This game is amazing! I've been following development through its early access (watched like all the JessiMew playthroughs she did) and the development team rlly took in the feedback and polished the game to what it is today.
The ui may be a bit hard to understand at first, and the tutorial is a bit sparse, but the fact that the mutation menu has locked items helps ease you into the multitude of genes that this game has.
I rlly like that they have genes that exist irl, including the mode of transmission (like with hemophilia being X-linked)!
The nicheling models are absolutely adorable too and you can make quite a fun variety!
It's a fun game loop for me, you travel island to island, mutate your nichelings to fit your new environment, rinse and repeat. I like inventing stories for each island, adding colorful gems to represent certain beliefs, tribes and other events (it's also nice that the game files let you add extra gem colors). There's a lot of food options, dangers and climates, making the game loop not feel repetitive.
I also like that it's turn based, giving you time to think through mutations, match ups and stories, it feels nice and calm.
All in all, if you're looking for a chill game with cute critters that you can evolve any way you like, look no further. This might just be the game for you <3

One of the most thoughtfully designed genetics games I've seen. The island travel mechanic solves population control in such a nice way that I bet most people who play don't even notice that was a hard game design problem. It's not super realistic, mainly in having single-gene controls for very complex traits like gills or spikes, but the departures from reality seem deliberately chosen to make the experience more enjoyable. The average person who plays this is still going to learn a lot from it. There's even an X-linked gene.
I also like that the game saves on exit automatically, so that don't have to remember to click "Save" all the time. So nice to have that taken care of. The rest of the game has similarly good attention to detail.
The survival aspect is interesting and cohesive, but maybe a bit on the easy side. Or perhaps I got distracted with the genes and didn't travel the islands as fast as intended. There's still more of the game I haven't reached, so I'll see.
This game had a lot of love poured into its creation, and it shows.

Well...I feel I don't really need to say much about my knowledge on this game with the ungodly amount of hours I've spent on it. So now that my years of hyperfixation has washed away I feel I can finally give a fair and non-biased review on this game.

So this game is all about micro-managing this ragtag group of creatures (called nichelings) in which they have to "evolve" to survive the environment they're currently living in. Sounds interesting in concept but there's just not enough genetics, traits. biomes, and challenges that actually push you to the limit in which your forced to become a specialized species. Meaning I could have a whole ass platypus living in a snowy biome if I so wished, doesn't make sense right? Welcome to Niche.

Genuinely sometimes I feel this is a game that could have had SO MUCH MORE content, like genuinely. More creatures that can randomly spawn, more trees, different grass. Maybe miscarriages due to certain factors when it comes to loss of food or events, nichelings having certain traits or personalities (ie, gluttonous making them eat more food than a normal nicheling, energetic making them have more energy than a normal nicheling, something that's not defined just by physical traits practically). More weather too, like thunderstorms or something. Various more patterns as well but that's just me being greedy. Anyway you get the point, this game just didn't reach its maximum potential before the devs decided no more updates to base game content.

It obviously has its merits for me to play this long, which is that the content it DOES have is good-

You can guide the genetics your nichelings will acquire by making them live in certain conditions to unlock said genes, making them all unique and have different strengths. Some are strong, some good at collecting, some good at swimming, truly a wide array of possibilities. The generations system is also very good (you have a family tree where you can trace where certain traits came from), the genetics aspect of the game is also solid, and everything marketed is truly present and enjoyable but afrer a while it just gets...repetitive and boring. Nothing is new, nothing is a challenge unless I deliberately handicap myself to do so. 

It's a good time passer game overall, I just wish this game reached the heights of greatness that I know it could have achieved. People who are neurodivergent will definitely enjoy (I am living proof). 10/10 game, wish they'd just add more content, hell I'd even take fantasy creature traits/genetics at this point

I'm a bit split on if I should recommend the game or not. The graphics are charming, it has a unique gameplay loop, the premise is interesting and the price is very affordable. And I'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy my first  two(?) playthroughs.

Above all else, however: I don't understand how anyone can find it overly challenging. It is *stupidly* easy to cheese the game by lingering on islands with abundant resources while not over-staying on challenging ones.  A sense of completionism, or more specifically, the unlocking of new genes is the only incentive to stick around on unique islands for any time longer than it takes you to cross them, but most traits are not going to be useful in the long run and once you realize the magic sort of disappears. (Arguably, the optimal strategy while playing is to maintain a large population of "generalists", with minimal adaptations to any given island.)

One pitfall new players can fall into is the assumption that you are supposed to entirely avoid inbreeding, when the game in fact incentivises it: Rogue males have horrible genetics, random encounters with new nichelings are unreliable AND much of the gameplay involves "curating" the genes of your nichelings, in short: the game expects you to mostly breed within your pack.  But that being said, unless you do a self-imposed challenge run, entirely neglect resource gathering or don't breed it's VERY hard to lose.

For as interesting of a game as it is conceptually, it is in my opinion a bit shallow in execution. Basically, one of those sandbox games which is fun for some time, but eventually gets pretty boring unless you add an element of personal roleplay and/or challenge. 

Worth buying if you find yourself intrigued, but go in with tempered expectations.

I really wanted to like this game. Theres a lot of heart and effort put into every aspect and the comunity around it has been so wonderful and passionate for YEARS. I followed the development since this game first started gaining traction and I was so excited tog et playing it.

When I finally got and started playing the game, thats when it all fell apart. It has good visuals, good ui design, good music, good art. Everything is amazing except for one aspect. The core gameplay loop. This game meshes two ideas that clash with each other. Its meant to be a strategic survival game. A limited amount of moves per day, units that each have different skills and abilities, natural hazards, and resources that need to be managed to survive and progress. The creatures you need to keep alive, though, are the main issue. They die of old age far too quickly, so getting attached to them or having them specialize in certain tasks is a recipe for disaster. Even the story seems to forget how fast they die off. It just clashes with the survival aspect, within a matter of a few days I have an entirely new cast that I just dont have enough time to even think about beyond their stats. If they stayed alive for just a little bit longer, then I could actually care about each individual and their lineage. If they stayed alive for just a little bit longer I could actually get invested, but I cant.

I tried five separate times to play this game and like it and every time I just fail. It just loses me. My guys will die in two days anyways so why should I even care about keeping them alive? Why should I care about getting back to the original tribe when the one guy who even knew about it died 30 generations ago? Even if it was for balancing purposes so you couldn't have too many kids with someone with op genes, just make them be infertile as they get older.

TLDR: The lifespans are too short for me to get invested in the survival or genetics of the creatures in this genetics survival game.

No feeling like the dread you get when you travel to a jungle world on story mode and have all of Adam's decendants get absolutely demolished by the different monkeys on the first day. 

Jokes aside, this game can be quite engaging. It combines strategy by adding the ability to add modifiers to hopefully create more nichelings with specific genetic traits. It mixes strategy and cute critters, and I think that's pretty neat. (It can get a tiny bit tedious, my word of advice is to keep your pack relatively small and collect as much food as you can. Don't go above like, 20 members, and that's pushing it.) solid 8.5/10 game, 10/10 if planning and strategy are your forte. 
The bearenas can be rough though lol watch out for them and use sniff/hearing to know for certain if they're accompanied by a baby or not. If you don't want any bearenas, even a friendly one, take out the baby in a few turns or else you'll be stuck with a full grown one in just a few days. (probably more useful for you to just befriend them though.)

if you want to learn more about the game in a fun and engaging way, try watching Seri! Pixel Biologist's videos on the game. She turns them into a story you can follow day by in-game day, and it helps you get a feel for the game. (This is how I got into the game initially.) These videos help not only get a feel for the mechanics but also can be a relaxing way to wind down.

This game I would definitely consider part of the "Stardew Valley" niche in that it is relaxing and is a game you can take at your own pace. If you happen to be a science nerd, you might really enjoy this game. There is strategy to getting specific genes for different areas, (such as venomous fangs for swamps or jungles, due to the dangers and poison berries.) Overall, really fun and engaging game, highly recommend to any science nerd who thinks genetics are pretty cool.

200 Spielstunden (einschließlich Idle-Zeiten) bedeuten: Ja, es hat gefallen. Die Nichlinge sind sehr niedlich und wirken trotz der begrenzten Animation auch sehr lebendig. Mir hat es viel Spaß gemacht, mit ihnen zu spielen, und die verschiedenen genetischen Entwürfe zu sehen. Man kann Niche als schnelle Survival-Reise spielen mit knappen Vorräten und hohem Überlebensdruck. Alternativ lässt sich auch eher Ressourcen-Management betreiben, was das Überleben auf schwierigen Inseln deutlich entschärft. Und auf freundlichen Inseln oder im Sandbox-Modus kann man sich ganz der Züchtung besonders schöner oder ungewöhnlicher Nichlinge widmen. Ich hätte mir im Spiel das ein oder andere Tool gewünscht, um meine Population besser im Blick behalten und Verpaarungen besser planen zu können. Aber so strategisch ist das Spiel eher nicht gedacht. ***

200 hours of playtime (including idle time) say it all: yes, I enjoyed it. The Nichelings are very cute and, despite the limited animation, feel surprisingly lively. I had a lot of fun playing with them and watching the different genetic designs emerge. Niche can be played as a fast-paced survival journey with scarce resources and constant pressure to survive. Alternatively, you can focus more on resource management, which makes survival on difficult islands much more manageable. And on friendly islands or in sandbox mode, you can fully devote yourself to breeding particularly beautiful or unusual Nichelings. I would have liked a few more tools to keep better track of my population and plan pairings more deliberately. But the game is not really meant to be that strategic. Just like in real life, the most optimal pairings don’t always happen 😊. A subtle sense of humor runs throughout the game and adds an extra touch of charm.
